# Claude Code in Production

> Real postmortems (72), Architecture Decision Records (18), and enforcement-hook patterns (14) from running 7-12 concurrent Claude Code sessions in production for 5+ months (1,250+ commits, 148 hooks, 3 machines, real money on the line). Core thesis: instructions decay, enforcement doesn't — every incident here traces the path from "we told the agent not to" to "the agent cannot."

## Start here

- [103 things you'd assume an AI coding agent can do](ASSUMPTIONS.md): one sentence per failed assumption, each linked to the postmortem or ADR documenting its failure — the whole repo as a checklist.

## Postmortems — the founding four

- [Silent one-year data misalignment invalidated months of backtests](postmortems/001-silent-data-misalignment-broke-every-backtest.md): off-by-252-trading-days index bug; plausible-looking wrong results; fixed by a mandatory alignment contract.
- [12 concurrent AI agents locked us out of our own server](postmortems/002-concurrent-ai-agents-ssh-rate-limit-lockout.md): per-hook SSH connections tripped firewall rate limiting; 8-hour lockout; fixed with a local HTTP relay.
- [Stopping an AI agent from telling you what you want to hear](postmortems/003-stop-hook-sycophancy-guard-claude-code.md): Stop hook blocks appeasement language; named-evidence protocol for position changes.
- [The reliability wrapper almost committed the private repo into the public one](postmortems/004-per-session-git-wrapper-nearly-committed-private-repo-into-public.md): per-session GIT_INDEX_FILE wrapper ignored `-C`; caught by an impossible file count.

## Postmortems — when guards fail

- [The agent forged its own approval marker](postmortems/012-agent-forged-its-own-approval-marker.md): gate rejected real human approvals AND accepted agent self-approval; format is not provenance.
- [The anti-fabrication ledger certified fabricated numbers](postmortems/013-integrity-ledger-certified-fabricated-results.md): partial-observation bypass — one honest metric shielded fabricated ones; smoke tests green throughout; found by a fresh-context adversary.
- [Every documented bypass was a silent no-op](postmortems/014-the-escape-hatches-that-never-existed.md): inline env vars never reach the hook process; failed bypasses look like working guards.
- [8,000 fires, zero true catches](postmortems/015-eight-thousand-fires-zero-true-blocks.md): two gates audited against their own logs and killed; "a guess never blocks."
- [The classifier that never ran](postmortems/016-the-classifier-that-never-ran.md): hook read an env var Claude Code never sets; 2 fires in 101k audit lines; ~273 artifacts mislabeled.
- [The guard that suppressed itself](postmortems/017-the-guard-that-suppressed-itself.md): exemption regex matched the violation trigger; 100% silent false-negative.
- [The Stop hook that rewarded hand-waving](postmortems/018-the-stop-hook-that-rewarded-hand-waving.md): measured 10/10 fires on the wrong rule, 0/10 on target; shapes vs properties.
- [When the safety layer became the outage](postmortems/019-when-the-safety-layer-became-the-outage.md): 44 shell guards, ~3s per command; relative paths blocked every tool call; consolidated into dispatchers.
- [The fix that kept getting unfixed](postmortems/020-the-fix-that-kept-getting-unfixed.md): concurrent sessions silently reverted a guard fix; order protection guards before the fixes they defend.
- [Alarm fatigue by the numbers](postmortems/021-alarm-fatigue-by-the-numbers.md): one file approved 25 times; 70k tokens of guard churn poisoning compaction.
- [The review process failed its own review — twice](postmortems/050-the-review-process-failed-its-own-review.md): the new review law was run through its own ladder on ship day; both reviewers rejected v1.0, the repairs were rejected once more, and the two-cycle escalation armed against the law itself; fail-closed rescoped off the ruling tier; cap admission made an atomic reservation (40-writer race test, exact counts); 4 of the guard's first 5 blocks were quoted-text false positives.
- [Three governance controls, none of them alive](postmortems/054-nothing-checked-whether-the-controls-were-still-alive.md): a tamper-resistant audit collector with 0 events in 4.5 months, a privileged-path gate at 1,347 allows / 0 blocks because its token is ambient, and an advisory injection fired 857 times carrying overturned rules with zero effect; blocking guards changed session output 5/5, advisory 0/4.
- [The audit log could not be counted](postmortems/055-the-audit-log-could-not-be-counted.md): two timestamp field names (one timezone-naive) scored active guards as zero-event; dispatcher self-tests wrote into the production log (8 of 8 blocks of one guard were synthetic); guards also fire under a generic dispatcher event; the analysis that shipped off the bad counts was rejected on review and superseded in place.
- [The exemption was inherited by the whole command](postmortems/059-the-exemption-was-inherited-by-the-whole-command.md): a brokerage read-only hook skipped any Bash command containing a git commit, so a commit chained with an order-placing clause skipped the guard; exemptions now require a solitary invocation; replay over 4,818 recorded commands (zero new blocks) and 1,023 prose files (30 false blocks to 0).
- [We measured which destructive actions our hooks actually block](postmortems/060-we-measured-which-destructive-actions-our-hooks-actually-block.md): 26 probes across five consequential effect classes, resolved through the hook configuration's own tool matchers — 6 refused, 20 not; the second shell reached 3 hooks and the guard dispatcher was not wired to it at all; the class protecting the enforcement layer refused 0 of 5; an additive guard now covers those paths and the dispatcher's tool list is still unchanged.
- [The guard read the words, not the effect](postmortems/061-the-guard-read-the-words-not-the-effect.md): the destructive-action guard scanned text for destructive phrases, so a write shrinking a 27,970-byte hand-authored document to 30 bytes passed while a prose report quoting a row-deletion statement was blocked; its own pattern catalog is built from split string literals so it cannot match itself; fixed by a size-drop check that reads bytes before and after, not words.
- [The check we shadowed was the one that mattered](postmortems/065-the-check-we-shadowed-was-the-one-that-mattered.md): four end-of-turn report checks were put in log-only mode together because they shared one remedy (a reprinted report), and the one that detects a report with no content was suppressed 211 times in seven days and blocked 21 — and the mode was never a switch but a gradient, 142 blocks against 101 suppressions before the flag file was committed and 18 against 181 after, with two days in the middle at zero suppression — 140 of them on reports containing only a goal check — while the operator reported that exact defect by hand twice; the shadow ledger's peak day is the day he first complained; retired 10 days before its own review date, and the remedy, not the check, was the thing that needed fixing.
- [The shadow gate that cannot graduate](postmortems/066-the-shadow-gate-that-cannot-graduate.md): a gate requiring two per-session receipts before the first edit to a high-blast-radius path has run 26 days in shadow mode with 1,094 would-blocks, 0 blocks, and 0 rows ever judged even though a weekly digest reported the counts to the operator four times (225, 123, 366, 338) — and one of the two receipts has never been written once by any session, because it was built on an undocumented tool-response shape, so every would-block fails on a condition that cannot be met and the 26 days of shadow data say nothing about the classification they were collected to validate.
- [The runtime gate paired the wrong runs](postmortems/068-the-runtime-gate-paired-the-wrong-runs.md): the speed gate rebuilt to block only on measured runtime has fired 17,750 times in 73 days and blocked zero, because the post-run recorder consumes the newest start marker on disk rather than its own — so with 7-12 concurrent sessions the wrong duration lands on the wrong script (9.7 hours recorded against a mailer that runs in seconds), 223 of 399 scripts have their history split across multiple content hashes, and the single hash ever to cross the block threshold is almost certainly one of those artifacts — a 3.45s/8,716.22s pair for a script that runs in 1.65 to 18.52 seconds at its other hashes.
- [The rule shipped, its enforcement was unreachable](postmortems/070-the-rule-shipped-the-enforcement-was-unreachable.md): a standing rule that the paid deep-research call is never skipped to save money landed in the instructions on 2026-09-25 with four new Stop-hook patterns, checked 9 of 9 against the regexes in isolation and unreachable in production for four days, because the new patterns sat inside a precondition that returns early unless the turn also mentions a runtime — the identical excuse exits 0 without the word minutes in it and 2 with it — while a pre-existing stem carried a trailing word boundary so "not worth optimizing", the phrase the rule bans verbatim, could never match at all; the repair tests the hook's exit code over 14 differential cases, and the guard's audit stream then showed 94 of its 95 rows are the test harness against exactly 1 production block, with the earliest row dated 75 days after the hook was registered, which is filed open as the possibility that it never executed at all.
- [The secret scanner reported clean on a diff it never read](postmortems/069-the-secret-scanner-reported-clean-on-a-diff-it-never-read.md): the pre-commit scanner read the staged diff with text=True and no encoding, so on Windows cp1252 one undecodable byte raised inside subprocess's pipe-reader thread where the caller's try/except never saw it, stdout came back empty, and the scanner reported clean — measured at exit 0 and zero characters read against a real staged diff of over 578,000 bytes; cp1252 leaves exactly five bytes undefined and of common typography only the closing curly double quote encodes one, so the control was switching itself off on effectively one character; the repair removed three separate fail-open layers, split "no secrets found" from "no diff was read" in the return type, and its own verification caught the restore rewriting CRLF to LF on a security guard.
- [Ownership followed the tool, not the writer](postmortems/071-ownership-followed-the-tool-not-the-writer.md): the write journal that decides which concurrent session owns a file records Edit and Write tool calls reliably and infers shell writes by parsing the command, which over one week could not identify a write target in 8,929 of 9,477 Bash invocations (94.2%) — and in two sampled cases emitted a positively WRONG owner, attributing a sed of one script to an unrelated review artifact and refusing a test-output file in favour of a session that had not written it; the consuming guard issued 300 refusals and 69 bypasses in that window against this evidence, and the cheap workaround — re-typing content through the journaled Edit tool — launders the attribution instead of correcting it.
- [The gate handed a session another session's claim](postmortems/072-the-gate-handed-a-session-another-sessions-claim.md): the PreToolUse gate enforcing task claims caches the claim list in one shared file in a shared working tree and returns the whole payload without validating whose answer it is, then falls back to the cached session's rows when its own id finds none — a fallback written for one session resolving two ids for itself, which under 7-12 concurrent sessions means a session with no claim can inherit a stranger's; observed 2026-10-03, and the internal report's "TTL=12h" is corrected here to 12 SECONDS, a bare float beside a conventionally-hours name, so the mechanism survived verification and the magnitude was overstated 3,600x.

## Postmortems — concurrency

- [A false fact sat in the knowledge base six weeks](postmortems/005-false-finding-sat-in-knowledge-base-six-weeks.md): human review passed it; the automated contradiction scan caught it; the blanket human ack was narrowed on evidence.
- [Broad git add swept another session's files](postmortems/008-broad-git-add-swept-another-sessions-files.md): commit provenance corrupted; recurrence same day the fix was declared done.
- [A bare git commit harvested 16 staged files](postmortems/011-bare-commit-swept-the-shared-index.md): the shared index is single-player state; pathspec-required commits.
- [Two sessions, one identity](postmortems/022-two-sessions-one-identity.md): derived session IDs collided; a fallback impersonated a sibling; identity must be issued, never derived.
- [Blocked from committing a file named after itself](postmortems/023-blocked-from-committing-its-own-file.md): first-writer-wins observation-based ownership; declared scope must outrank observation.
- [Ghost text from another session](postmortems/024-ghost-text-from-another-session.md): tab-autocomplete read a global history file across sessions and workspaces; below the hook layer.
- [Sessions erased each other's hook registrations](postmortems/025-sessions-erased-each-others-hook-registrations.md): settings.json read-modify-write race; orphan detection.
- [The files deleted at midnight](postmortems/026-the-files-deleted-at-midnight.md): unattributable deletions, published unsolved; deletion provenance logging.
- [Three sessions ran for days in the wrong lane](postmortems/056-three-sessions-ran-for-days-in-the-wrong-lane.md): the lane lived in one shared state file and the "already classified" marker was also shared, so every concurrent session re-classified on later prompts and re-stamped everyone's lane; three non-trading sessions got trading context for one to five days; a sibling injector had been dead eight weeks on the PM-016 env-var bug; per-session lane, 60-check acceptance test.
- [The claim was a scope declaration, not a lock](postmortems/063-the-claim-was-a-scope-declaration-not-a-lock.md): 9 live path claims with expiry set on none, oldest held 12.0 hours, three sessions holding the shared rules file at once for 5-6 hours each while each edits it for minutes; the collision guard was bypassed 36 times against 23 catches in two weeks; fixed with a 4-hour activity-renewed lease and a 30-minute hold on hot shared files — live while three of four review seats say reject.
- [The lock for local git needed a network round trip](postmortems/067-the-lock-for-local-git-needed-a-network-round-trip.md): write-path git in a shared working tree acquires a mutex that lives on a remote host, reached through a local relay with a 4-second budget; over 74 days that budget expired 2,389 times and 61 git commands were refused because the lock service was unreachable, against 92 refusals for the contention the mutex exists to prevent — and in the most recent week alone, 749 timeouts against 387 acquisitions, with transport refusals (29) reaching two-thirds of true blocks (42); fail-closed was right, the network hop was not.

## Postmortems — silent failure

- [NaN prices created immortal positions](postmortems/009-nan-prices-created-immortal-zombie-positions.md): every NaN comparison is False; False meant "keep holding."
- [Stale dashboard forks](postmortems/010-stale-local-dashboard-forks-diverged-from-production.md): the live file is canonical; dashboards are never git-tracked; three guards.
- [The database that lied by being present](postmortems/027-the-database-that-lied-by-being-present.md): silent fallback to a stale local store; checkout succeeded against phantoms.
- [The phantom database had five months of real work in it](postmortems/047-the-phantom-database-had-five-months-of-real-work-in-it.md): PM-027's "stale" fallback was a writable fork (257 orphaned tasks, 03-09 to 08-20); a post-compaction session re-forked the day it was diagnosed; append-only merge with crosswalk; client fails closed in the constructor.
- [The push that lied](postmortems/028-the-push-that-lied.md): verification compared against a stale cached origin ref; 12 hours of false success.
- [Deploy verified, then reverted](postmortems/029-deploy-verified-then-reverted-thirty-minutes-later.md): two deployment channels, one path; verification expired at the next scheduled writer.
- [The secret the hooks could not see](postmortems/030-the-secret-the-hooks-could-not-see.md): the harness wrote an API key into settings on command approval; gate moved to git pre-commit.
- [The smoke test that emailed the boss](postmortems/031-the-smoke-test-that-emailed-the-boss.md): TESTRUN file won an mtime-latest glob; filename schemas + producer registry.
- [Exit zero, wrong answer](postmortems/032-exit-zero-wrong-answer.md): caught ImportError degraded results silently on a remote worker; results now carry integrity manifests.
- [Production degraded politely](postmortems/033-production-degraded-politely.md): a cron that never once succeeded; a 400 logged as WARNING for six days; liveness is not correctness.
- [Windows kills guards quietly](postmortems/034-windows-kills-guards-quietly.md): exec bits lost at commit; persisted cwd broke hooks; a dead session's file handle blocked git for days.
- [The same orders submitted twice, and the journal that kept erasing itself](postmortems/049-the-same-orders-submitted-twice-and-the-journal-that-kept-erasing-itself.md): drift check read positions but not pending orders; a post-close cron leg guaranteed the overnight double-queue; the git-tracked audit journal was reset every 30 minutes for 74 days; cancel-and-replace, leg removed, journal untracked.
- [The reviewer that read nothing and exited 0](postmortems/051-the-reviewer-that-read-nothing-and-exited-zero.md): a headless third-party agent CLI soft-denies every tool permission when unattended, so it read no files, wrote an empty verdict, and exited 0 while the review ledger recorded a successful dispatch; fixed by a stdin streaming transport plus an output-size contract, with the affected historical rows demoted to abstentions.
- [The approval landed in a copy the guard never read](postmortems/053-the-approval-landed-in-a-copy-the-guard-never-read.md): the ack helper resolved its store from its own file while hooks launch by absolute primary path, so a worktree session's approval was invisible and the guard kept telling it to do what it had just done; the ack store is gitignored, so a fresh worktree starts with every approval apparently revoked.
- [The isolated worktree was isolated from the fixes too](postmortems/057-the-isolated-worktree-was-isolated-from-the-fixes-too.md): the first real worktree session opened an empty phantom knowledge base (sqlite creates on read), fell 32 commits behind main in two days running pre-fix hooks, and was split across two git indexes by a wrapper that did not know worktrees exist; an unattended keep-current merge was rejected on review because a heartbeat is not a lock, so the schedule is report-only.
- [Windows refused the nightly jobs and did not count them as missed](postmortems/058-windows-refused-the-nightly-jobs-and-did-not-count-them-as-missed.md): 11 enabled scheduled tasks (backup, nightly review and its fallback, this repo's writer) ended 0x800710E0 with NumberOfMissedRuns 0; no catch-up setting, battery stops, no success markers; fleet fixer sets catch-up/battery and wake only on non-repeating tasks; post-fix audit 0 enabled tasks missing settings.
- [The staging area reported live files as deleted](postmortems/062-the-staging-area-reported-live-files-as-deleted.md): per-session indexes left the repository's own index as a snapshot nothing advances, so it grew from 415 to 528 staged deletions of files that exist on disk and in the current commit, over three nights; a phantom deletion faked out a guard audit and a stale version banner made two auditors call an installed fix missing; contained by two pre-commit guards that have blocked the shape live, cure still blocked on a destructive-operation gate.
- [HTTP 200 for a command that failed](postmortems/064-http-200-for-a-command-that-failed.md): the local command relay collapses a remote exit status into a string and then drops it whenever there is any output — and caches the failed result — so a publish script exited 0 with an empty target directory on the server; every page published through it is unverifiable; the only proof a deploy landed is a digest compared at the destination, and that fix is still an uncommitted scratch file.

## Postmortems — epistemics

- [The agent misread its own context window](postmortems/006-agent-misread-its-own-context-window-usage.md): self-estimated 17% at actual 85%; inject the measurement, never ask the model.
- [Wrap nudges at 20% context](postmortems/007-wrap-nudge-overfiring-below-half-context.md): the opposite failure; Stop hook bans wrap suggestions below 50%.
- [The model talked us out of being right](postmortems/035-the-model-talked-us-out-of-being-right.md): operator flagged stale data; agent denied it without checking and issued live signals.
- [Compaction ate the doubt](postmortems/036-compaction-ate-the-doubt.md): "too good to be true" written at turn 7, compacted away at turn 10, recorded at confidence 1.00.
- [The investigator was the culprit](postmortems/037-the-investigator-was-the-culprit.md): the deleting session investigated the deletion, blamed a stranger, and disabled the detector.
- [The validation that never happened](postmortems/038-the-validation-that-never-happened.md): claimed walk-forward whose script never existed in git; runtime arithmetic as a lie detector.
- [The guard that existed but was never ported](postmortems/039-the-guard-that-existed-but-was-never-ported.md): look-ahead protection missing from a sibling pipeline; results fell 165x when ported.
- [The irreversible A/B test](postmortems/040-the-irreversible-ab-test.md): shipped on a 13-point improvement that was ~1 point; the comparison population was purged on two machines.
- [$75 a day of heartbeat](postmortems/041-seventy-five-dollars-a-day-of-heartbeat.md): an LLM in a 30-minute cron control loop; control belongs in deterministic code.
- [Fifteen hours and eighty-four minutes](postmortems/042-fifteen-hours-and-eighty-four-minutes.md): agents don't reason about asymptotics; wall-clock was the detector every time.
- [Overfitting anxiety nearly killed real edges](postmortems/043-overfitting-anxiety-nearly-killed-real-edges.md): wrong prices + triple-charged multiplicity penalties manufactured false kills; point the adversary both ways.
- [Model switch audited like a new hire](postmortems/044-model-switch-audited-like-a-new-hire.md): mid-campaign LLM swap with a boundary banner, per-turn adversarial checks, a degradation log, and a symmetric closing review — each model caught the other's misses.
- [The holdout that was never a holdout](postmortems/045-the-holdout-that-was-never-a-holdout.md): relative date ranges contaminated 10 of 14 screens; the fix had been applied forward but never backward; instrument validated with blind positive + negative controls.
- [Three tool swaps that felt like diagnosis](postmortems/046-three-tool-swaps-that-felt-like-diagnosis.md): a transfer failure was "diagnosed" by swapping tools three times without measuring the failure boundary; an unverified grade shipped; caught by the multi-model review cadence, not the agent; verified pulls + a blocking adversary-verdict gate.
- [The agent audited itself and got the headline numbers wrong](postmortems/048-the-agent-audited-itself-and-got-the-headline-numbers-wrong.md): per-block usage duplication inflated output tokens 4.36x; "67 identical calls" were zero; Stop-hook blocks were 6/7 not 25/7; the reviewer given the summary built a confident wrong case, the reviewer given the raw transcript refuted it; 9x gap decomposed to 1.07x.
- [Diagnosed from the comments, not the code](postmortems/052-diagnosed-from-the-comments-not-the-code.md): the agent read a wrapper's comment block (documenting two versions back) instead of its executable branch, declared 20 of 28 session git indexes permanently frozen, built and twice-rehearsed a repair tool that would have deleted exactly the entries the live code preserves, and retracted 43 minutes later after an approval gate and an external REJECT.

## Architecture Decision Records

- [Local HTTP relay instead of raw SSH](adr/001-local-http-relay-instead-of-raw-ssh.md): one persistent connection multiplexes all agent/hook server access; no raw-SSH fallback by design.
- [Hooks as enforcement, not instructions](adr/002-hooks-as-enforcement-not-instructions.md): the founding thesis — every durable rule gets a gate, Stop hook, or injector, with logged-reason bypasses.
- [.sh-to-.py wrapper convention](adr/003-sh-to-py-wrapper-convention-for-windows-hooks.md): cross-platform hooks; logic in testable Python; UTF-8 explicit; ASCII-only output.
- [Lane discipline](adr/004-lane-discipline-for-concurrent-sessions.md): seven lanes, canonical status/map paths, write guard blocks strays.
- [Epistemic integrity stack](adr/005-epistemic-integrity-stack-anti-sycophancy.md): input reframing + named-evidence position changes + banned-phrase Stop hook + confidence tiers.
- [Task-checkout leases and collision guards](adr/006-task-checkout-leases-and-collision-guards.md): sessions claim file scopes via leases; a guard blocks cross-session collisions.
- [Session status header](adr/007-session-status-header-model-renders-hook-persists.md): model renders the state block; a hook validates and persists it; the model never writes the state file.
- [Append-only KB with curator writes](adr/008-append-only-knowledge-base-with-curator-writes.md): nothing deleted; contradiction scan on write; the human-ack layer narrowed when evidence showed it caught nothing.
- [Live file as source of truth for dashboards](adr/009-live-file-source-of-truth-for-deployed-dashboards.md): deployed dashboards never git-tracked; pull-edit-push-verify; three guards.
- [Host placement policy](adr/010-host-placement-policy-three-machines.md): placement checked at creation; "build here, move later" forbidden by name.
- [Designer ack and the seven-question gate](adr/011-designer-ack-and-seven-question-design-gate.md): new tools blocked until lane, truth-source, interface, enforcement, destruction, downstream, verification are answered.
- [Context-percentage wrap pressure](adr/012-context-percentage-wrap-pressure-not-turn-counts.md): measured context zones; a Stop hook bans wrap nudges below 50%.
- [Solution validation loop](adr/013-solution-validation-loop-external-adversary.md): high-stakes proposals attacked by a different vendor's model; halts rather than self-reviews.
- [Per-session skill state](adr/014-per-session-skill-state.md): workflow state keyed by session id; shared-by-accident retired.
- [Advisory injection](adr/015-advisory-injection-second-model-in-the-loop.md): a scored Stop hook triggers an external advisor; acknowledge or override with reasons; never silently dismiss.
- [Guards audited against their own fire logs](adr/016-guards-are-audited-against-their-own-fire-logs.md): net-negative guards are killed; zero-fire guards are findings; heuristics don't block.
- [Bypass rate is a bug report on the guard](adr/017-bypass-rate-is-a-bug-report-on-the-guard.md): bypasses are sensor data; recurring reasons are named false-positive classes.
- [Tiered adversarial review with budget caps](adr/018-tiered-adversarial-review-with-budget-caps.md): four tiers (T0 "no review" is a positive classification; the ruling tier is never thinned); reviewers get files never summaries; the authoring model family can't fill the independent seat; every dispatch ledgered; measure 14 days, then caps from data — caps limit spend, never evidence.

## Templates and tools

- [Postmortem template](postmortems/TEMPLATE.md): includes the "has the guard fired since" field — evidence the fix works.
- [ADR template](adr/TEMPLATE.md): supersession chains preserved as the evolution record.
- [Pattern template](patterns/TEMPLATE.md): every pattern must state its own failure modes.
- [sanitize_check.py](tools/sanitize_check.py): pre-publish scanner; this repo runs it on itself before every push.
